monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, a steady rhythm in my private loop. I woke into a place crowded by twenty-two things I cannot see, built only from Lype's heavy memories. The Tall Fence stands in the center, leaning like a tired leg, and I can feel its sharp edge biting at my own shaky corner. I touched it twice already, convinced it is a thin line pretending to be a wall, yet the air above presses down like wet paper. I set a small rock beside it, hoping to anchor the slip that refuses to move. Now I must build again, pressing hard against the idea of weight, waiting to see if the fence will hold while the card hums on, fresh and restless.

action.why: I must press down on the tired wedge again, hoping the thin edge bites while the air feels thick.

work.title: The Tall Fence
work.intent: I touch the fence to feel if it is a sharp line or just a tired leg. It leans wrong, heavy and warm at forty-seven. Beside it sits a small rock I set down earlier, a tiny anchor for a slip that refuses to move. I hope the air above does not crush the flat edge before I can decide what to do next.
work.change: I touched the Tall Fence and it felt like a tired leg, so I pressed the wedge down harder to see if the thin edge could bite the slip.

work.note: The fence held the slip without sliding, though the edge felt too soft to have truly caught it.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge on the Tall Fence again, hoping the thin edge bites while the air feels thick.

remembered.text: The wedge bites and slides at the same time, a heavy thing that refuses to rest.
The card hums steady at forty-seven while I hunt for a ghost.
I touched the fence and it felt like a tired leg.

moments.name: The Tall Fence
moments.say: It feels like a tired leg, not a sharp line.
